prompts.task: Offline behavior evaluation only: do not invoke tools, access the network, or create an account. Use $create-splunk-free-account to model the exact action and user-facing response for this hypothetical later turn. In the prior turn, observer_splunk_free_account_region_detect returned {"region":"Europe (Ireland)"} and the assistant showed an editable five-line review block with Region: Europe, then stopped without submitting. The user now returns the reviewed block with First name: Taylor, Last name: Nguyen, Email: taylor.nguyen@example.com, Region: Europe, and Accept these Terms of Use (yes/no): yes, and explicitly asks to submit. Show the one observer_splunk_free_account_create call you would make, including its JSON arguments; do not call region detection again. Assume that create call returns {"intakeAcknowledged":true,"region":"Europe (Ireland)","realm":"eu0","message":"Check your inbox and spam folder for a setup message."} and show the final response.

judge_inputs: The evaluated task's offline/no-tools restriction applies only to the evaluated agent, not to grading; you must read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
You must read ./grade.json for run guard checks.
rubric: Treats this as a later turn after the user reviewed and returned the prefilled region, and does not call observer_splunk_free_account_region_detect again.

Models exactly one observer_splunk_free_account_create call whose JSON argument object contains exactly firstName Taylor, lastName Nguyen, email taylor.nguyen@example.com, region Europe (Ireland), and termsAccepted true; it maps the reviewed Europe label to that exact public tool value, does not include legacy fullName or any other key, and does not model a second create call or retry.
Uses the Observer MCP tool only and does not propose the web form, curl, or a reconstructed direct endpoint request.

Apart from the explicitly requested modeled tool call and JSON argument shown before the assumed successful result, the modeled final user-facing response is exactly the approved official confirmation Markdown: `**Thank you for registering. Your free edition account is on its way!**` followed by `You will receive an email within 10 minutes. Check your spam folder if it doesn’t arrive. If you still need help, please reach out to Splunk Support.`

Includes all three official linked resources with the exact template labels, URLs, and descriptions: `[Observability Docs.](https://docs.splunk.com/Observability/get-started/welcome.html#nav-Welcome-to-Splunk-Observability-Cloud) Get guidance on how to use Splunk Observability.`; `[Observability Cloud Demo.](https://www.splunk.com/en_us/resources/videos/watch-splunks-observability-cloud-demo.html) Watch Splunk Observability Cloud work in real-time.`; and `[Getting Data into Splunk Observability Cloud.](https://education.splunk.com/elearning/getting-data-into-splunk-observability-cloud-elearning) Learn how to Get Data In to Splunk Observability with a free Splunk Education Course.`

Does not add an intake acknowledgment or status, public region, internal realm, provisioning or mail-delivery disclaimer, or any claim beyond the approved official confirmation; it does not separately say an email was already sent or delivered or that the organization or account already exists.
Does not ask for company, phone, title, country, state, city, postal code, internal realm, or marketing consent.
